newsitem.title: UK: Amnesty accuses Taleban of reign of terror.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty accuses Taleban of reign of terror.

text.p: Amnesty International accused the new rulers of Afghanistan on Wednesday of conducting a reign of terror and said the radical Islamic Taleban militia have taken up to 1,000 prisoners during house-to-house searches in the capital.
The human rights organisation said it feared that civilians suspected of being sympathisers of ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani could be tortured or killed.
"Despite statements from their leadership suggesting moderation, it is clear that Taleban guards are busily implementing a reign of terror in Kabul," Amnesty said in a statement.
"Families are afraid to go out into the streets, afraid to answer their doors and afraid that their loved ones will suffer the brutal consequence of being found "un-Islamic' by the militia."
Taleban forces, which overtook Kabul last Friday and now control three-quarters of Afghanistan, are on the brink of a battle with the forces of former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.
Amnesty said that children and women were also being ill-treated by militia guards. In some areas girls' schools have been closed and women have not been allowed to leave their homes.

"Under the Taleban's code, women have been ordered to give up their rights as citizens equal to men," the group said. "Some women who have defied the Taleban's orders have already been brutally beaten in public by guards wielding long chains."
